title: Dead faith can be called true or not by respect; only charity-animated faith truly profits
source_text: IX. Agnoscunt tamen fidem mortuam & informem diverso sensu & respectu posse dici veram & non veram, & verae fidei titulum posse ad fidem formatam restringi. Ut praesertim videre est apud authorem illum qui in Reformatos nuper insectus est tanquam Christianam Ethicen subvertentes. Notat enim in rebus verum saepe sumi pro eo quod est in perfectionis sibi debitae statu. Ita verum Regem dici qui facit quod in se est ut regnum suum recte administret: verum Episcopum illum qui continuo gregis sibi commissi saluti invigilat: verum Christianum qui vivit ut Christiano homine dignum est. Sed tamen non esse nomen veri Regis simpliciter denegandum illi qui, quamvis Rex legitimus sit, Regis officio non recte fungitur, veri Episcopi illi qui rite vocatus atque ordinatus non implet partes boni Episcopi, & veri Christiani illi, qui Christi Baptismate tinctus, & Christianae doctrinae mysteriis omnibus non simulate credens, indulget operibus carnis, nec vitam agit suae professioni respondentem. Unde concludit, quamvis quod superest fidei in Christianis illis, qui ex accepta in Baptismo gratia, non per infidelitatem, sed per alia peccata exciderunt, vera fides sit & dici debeat, bono sensu tamen dici posse eam solam fidem esse veram, quae est per charitatem animata: quoniam scilicet ea sola est quae nobis prodest, quae nos reddit Dei filios, & Christum in cordibus nostris habitare facit. Quod postea multis Patrum testimoniis probat, & ex publico ipso Officio Ecclesiae Romanae.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they acknowledge that dead and unformed faith can in a diverse sense and respect be called true and not true, and that the title of true faith can be restricted to formed faith. As may be seen especially in that author who lately attacked the Reformed as subverting Christian ethics. For he notes that in things true is often taken for that which is in the state of perfection due to it. Thus a true King is said who does what is in him that he may administer his kingdom rightly: a true Bishop he who continually watches for the salvation of the flock committed to him: a true Christian who lives as is worthy of a Christian man. Yet the name of a true King is not simply to be denied to him who, although he is a legitimate King, does not rightly discharge the office of King, nor of a true Bishop to him who, duly called and ordained, does not fulfill the parts of a good Bishop, nor of a true Christian to him who, baptized with Christ's Baptism and believing all the mysteries of Christian doctrine not by pretense, indulges the works of the flesh and does not lead a life answering to his profession. Whence he concludes that although what remains of faith in those Christians who fell from grace received in Baptism not by unbelief but by other sins is and ought to be called true faith, yet in a good sense it can be said that that alone is true faith which is animated by charity: because namely that alone is what profits us, which makes us sons of God, and makes Christ dwell in our hearts. Which afterward he proves by many testimonies of the Fathers, and from the public Office itself of the Roman Church.
pass_b_english: Rome allows dead faith to be called true or not by respect, and can reserve the title of true faith for formed faith.
The Ethicen opponent's analogy: a legitimate king, bishop, or baptized believer may still fail the perfection due to the name — yet the name is not simply denied.

So faith left in those who fell from baptismal grace by other sins than unbelief is true faith; yet in a good sense only charity-animated faith is called true, because that alone profits, makes us God's children, and seats Christ in the heart — backed by Fathers and Rome's public Office.

lemmas.gloss: in a diverse sense and respect

choices.english: true faith ... in a good sense
choices.why: Dual respect on dead faith's truth.
rejected: dead faith never true in any sense
